feedback.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=0$ for the curve $r(t)=⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(0),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡0-0\operatorname{sin}⁡0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡0+0\operatorname{cos}⁡0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(0) & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡0-0\operatorname{cos}⁡0,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡0-0\operatorname{sin}⁡0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(0)$ and ${r}^{″}(0)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0) & =⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,2,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =2k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖ & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{{1}^{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
